title: Reported speech 3
use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty shell. 30 items, inside the 24-40 band. Two predecessors already own the mechanics and neither is repeated: b1_reported_speech (54) has backshift, said/told and if/wh reporting, and b1_reported_speech_2 (25) has the word order of a reported question and reported commands and requests. Between them *say*, *tell* and *ask* are finished. What is left, and what a B2 student cannot do, is the REPORTING VERBS THEMSELVES and the pattern each one demands — the classic FCE area. Two blocks, deliberately different jobs. The PATTERN block (12) gives the verb and gaps what follows it, lemma cued (B11): *He admitted ____ the money. (take)*, with the other three patterns as distractors on the same lemma (B6). The VERB block (12) does the reverse and solves A0 the only honest way: the DIRECT SPEECH IS PRINTED IN THE STEM, so exactly one reporting verb fits — *'It was not me.' -> He ____ taking the money* can only be *denied*. Without that stem the item would accept four answers. Use is error-correction (E7) on the six real Czech-learner pattern errors: *admitted to take*, *suggested to go*, *refused paying*, *apologised to be late*, *insisted to pay*, *advised me seeing*. NO gap_class here, and that is deliberate rather than the earlier miss: these gaps are verb-pattern forms, not grammar words, and FCE-EXERCISES scopes gap_class to prepositions, conjunctions, articles, pronouns, auxiliaries, quantifiers and relatives. Same reasoning as b2_suffixes_1. A8 accepts generated as a contraction closure; D1 every item names its own verb and its own pattern.

cards.title: Reported speech 3
points: *Say*, *tell* and *ask* are finished. English has many more reporting verbs.
Each one chooses **one** pattern, and the pattern is not guessable.
The verb you choose says what kind of speech act it was.

cards.title: You already know
points: Reported speech 1 gave you backshift and said/told.
Reported speech 2 gave you reported questions and commands.
Here the machinery is the same — only the **verb** and its pattern are new.

cards.title: Verbs that take -ing
points: These four never take *to* + verb. This is the commonest mistake in the unit.

cards.title: Verbs that take to + verb
points: Some take *to* straight away; others need a **person** first.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Czech uses one clause for all of these, so the English pattern has to be learned per verb.

items.en: She offered to help me with the boxes.
items.cz: Nabídla se, že mi pomůže s krabicemi.
items.gap: She offered ____ me with the boxes. (help)
accepts: She offered to help me with the boxes.

items.en: He admitted taking the money.
items.gap: He admitted ____ the money. (take)
accepts: He admitted taking the money.

items.en: They refused to pay the extra cost.
items.gap: They refused ____ the extra cost. (pay)
accepts: They refused to pay the extra cost.

items.en: She denied breaking the window.
items.gap: She denied ____ the window. (break)
accepts: She denied breaking the window.

items.en: He promised to call me the next day.
items.cz: Slíbil, že mi druhý den zavolá.
items.gap: He promised ____ me the next day. (call)
accepts: He promised to call me the next day.
items.explanation: **promise** takes **to** + verb. Note *the next day*, not *tomorrow*.
items.explanation_cz: **promise** má **to** + sloveso. Všimni si *the next day*, ne *tomorrow*.

items.en: We suggested going by train.
items.gap: We suggested ____ by train. (go)
accepts: We suggested going by train.

items.en: She apologised for being late.
items.gap: She apologised ____ late. (be)
accepts: She apologised for being late.

items.en: He insisted on paying for dinner.
items.cz: Trval na tom, že večeři zaplatí.
items.gap: He insisted ____ for dinner. (pay)
accepts: He insisted on paying for dinner.

items.en: They advised me to see a doctor.
items.cz: Poradili mi, ať jdu k lékaři.
items.gap: They advised me ____ a doctor. (see)
accepts: They advised me to see a doctor.

items.en: She reminded me to lock the door.
items.gap: She reminded me ____ the door. (lock)
accepts: She reminded me to lock the door.

items.en: He warned us not to swim there.
items.gap: He warned us ____ there. (swim)
accepts: He warned us not to swim there.
items.explanation: The negative sits before *to*: **not to swim**.

items.en: She invited us to stay for dinner.
items.cz: Pozvala nás, ať zůstaneme na večeři.
items.gap: She invited us ____ for dinner. (stay)
accepts: She invited us to stay for dinner.

items.en: She apologised for being late.
items.gap: 'I am sorry I was late.' -> She ____ for being late.
accepts: She apologised for being late.
items.explanation: *I am sorry* is an apology, so **apologised**.

items.en: He denied taking the money.
items.gap: 'It was not me.' -> He ____ taking the money.
accepts: He denied taking the money.
items.explanation: *It was not me* is a denial: **denied** + -ing.

items.en: He admitted taking the money.
items.gap: 'Yes, I took it.' -> He ____ taking the money.
accepts: He admitted taking the money.
items.explanation: *Yes, I took it* is a confession: **admitted** + -ing.

items.en: She suggested going by train.
items.gap: 'Shall we go by train?' -> She ____ going by train.
accepts: She suggested going by train.

items.en: He offered to help.
items.gap: 'I will help you.' -> He ____ to help.
accepts: He offered to help.
items.explanation: An unasked-for *I will help* is an offer: **offered** to help.
items.explanation_cz: Nevyžádané *I will help* je nabídka: **offered** to help.

items.en: She refused to pay.
items.gap: 'No, I will not pay.' -> She ____ to pay.
accepts: She refused to pay.
items.explanation: *No, I will not* is a refusal: **refused** to pay.
items.explanation_cz: *No, I will not* je odmítnutí: **refused** to pay.

items.en: He promised to call.
items.gap: 'I promise I will call.' -> He ____ to call.
accepts: He promised to call.
items.explanation: **promised** to call — the speaker gave his word.

items.en: He warned us not to swim there.
items.gap: 'Do not swim there — it is dangerous.' -> He ____ us not to swim there.
accepts: He warned us not to swim there.
items.explanation: Danger plus an instruction is a warning: **warned**.

items.en: She advised me to see a doctor.
items.cz: Poradila mi, ať jdu k lékaři.
items.gap: 'You should see a doctor.' -> She ____ me to see a doctor.
accepts: She advised me to see a doctor.
items.explanation: *You should…* is advice: **advised** me to see.
items.explanation_cz: *You should…* je rada: **advised** me to see.

items.en: She reminded me to lock the door.
items.gap: 'Do not forget to lock the door.' -> She ____ me to lock the door.
accepts: She reminded me to lock the door.
items.explanation: *Do not forget* is a reminder: **reminded** me to lock.
items.explanation_cz: *Do not forget* je připomínka: **reminded** me to lock.

items.en: She invited us to stay for dinner.
items.cz: Pozvala nás, ať zůstaneme na večeři.
items.gap: 'Would you like to stay for dinner?' -> She ____ us to stay.
accepts: She invited us to stay for dinner.
items.explanation: *Would you like to…?* is an invitation: **invited** us to stay.
items.explanation_cz: *Would you like to…?* je pozvání: **invited** us to stay.

items.en: He insisted on paying for dinner.
items.cz: Trval na tom, že večeři zaplatí.
items.gap: 'No, I really must pay.' -> He ____ on paying for dinner.
accepts: He insisted on paying for dinner.
items.explanation: Refusing to be talked out of it is **insisted** on + -ing.
items.explanation_cz: Když se nenechá odradit, je to **insisted** on + -ing.

items.en: He admitted taking the money.
items.wrong: He admitted to take the money.
accepts: He admitted taking the money.

items.en: We suggested going by train.
items.wrong: We suggested to go by train.
accepts: We suggested going by train.

items.en: They refused to pay the extra cost.
items.wrong: They refused paying the extra cost.
accepts: They refused to pay the extra cost.

items.en: She apologised for being late.
accepts: She apologised for being late.

items.en: He insisted on paying for dinner.
items.cz: Trval na tom, že večeři zaplatí.
items.wrong: He insisted to pay for dinner.
accepts: He insisted on paying for dinner.

items.en: She advised me to see a doctor.
items.cz: Poradila mi, ať jdu k lékaři.
items.wrong: She advised me seeing a doctor.
accepts: She advised me to see a doctor.
items.explanation: **advise** takes a person then **to** + verb: *advised me to see*.
items.explanation_cz: **advise** má osobu a pak **to** + sloveso: *advised me to see*.
